goal: `mc deps [<repo>]` answers, in one screen, which of a repository's dependencies need updating and how urgently: npm's outdated and audit readings of the lockfile on `origin/main`, merged per direct dependency into three groups — security fixable within the dependency's major, patch/minor behind, and major behind — each row marked runtime or tool, with the repository's own declared one-line notes (memoro: the wrangler release tally) as their own lines.

`mc deps bump <repo> security|minor|<package>[@<version>]` turns one of those groups into a pull request without anybody touching a checkout: a fresh workarea on `origin/main`, `package.json` and `package-lock.json` changed by npm with `--package-lock-only`, one commit, `mc publish`, then the ordinary `mc merge <repo> <pr>` gate round.
`mc deploy` says the reading in one line before its question — `mc: deps — 2 critical, 24 high; wrangler 4.116.0 → 4.149.0 (33 minor behind; D=2 S=1)` — from what `mc deps` last saved, with its age.
contract: Martin, 2026-10-09, at the brief: "Ja, bra, lägg upp mc deps som ett eget projekt" — to the sketch of a report in three groups with runtime/tool marked and the wrangler tally as its own row, a bump in its own workarea through the merge gate, and one deps line in `mc deploy`'s reading (ruling 29).

What is read is `origin/main`, after `git fetch origin main`: `package.json` and `package-lock.json` by `git show origin/main:<file>`, written into a fresh directory under `runnerScratchDir()` (`src/mc/paths.js`) and read there. Never the primary checkout's working tree and never any workarea's — `~/memoro` and `~/memoro-cli` are only the repositories whose refs are read. The one exception is a declared note command (step 1), which runs in the primary checkout because that is where the repository's own script lives.

Runtime or tool is decided by the section of `package.json` on `origin/main` and by nothing else: a name in `dependencies`, `optionalDependencies` or `peerDependencies` is `runtime`, a name in `devDependencies` is `tool`. A transitive package an audit flags is classified by the direct dependencies that pull it in (npm audit's `effects`, walked up to entries with `isDirect: true`): `runtime` if any of them is, else `tool`. A wrong-looking label (wrangler reads `tool`) is fixed by moving the package in `package.json`, never by a list in mc.

`npm outdated` is not used: measured 2026-10-09 against memoro's `origin/main` manifest and lockfile with no `node_modules`, it listed 32 of the 63 direct dependencies, no `devDependencies` and no `current`. The installed version is the lockfile's `packages["node_modules/<name>"].version`; the newest version within the same major is the last entry of `npm view <name>@^<installed> version --json` (a string when there is one match, an array sorted ascending otherwise — `^` on a `0.x` version is the same minor, which is what "same major" means for 0.x); the newest of all is `npm view <name> dist-tags.latest`. The audit is `npm audit --json --package-lock-only` in the scratch directory (measured 2.9 s on memoro).

`mc deps bump` never installs a `node_modules` anywhere, never runs `npm audit fix --force`, never touches the primary checkout, never merges anything but through `mc merge <repo> <pr>` and never deploys. Every npm write it makes carries `--package-lock-only`, because memoro's workareas hold `package-links` attachments into an immutable shared cache (`scripts/testing/dependency-cache.mjs` in memoro) and an install there would write through the links.
A group (`security`, `minor`) never crosses a major. Only an explicitly named `<package>@<version>` may, and the gate round is what decides whether it lands.
`mc deploy` makes no network call and no npm call for its deps line, and the line never refuses, delays or changes a deploy.
out_of_scope: memoro's own predeploy scripts — `scripts/wrangler-reminder.sh`, `scripts/check-wrangler.mjs`, `scripts/wrangler-bump.mjs` and the `predeploy` entry in its `package.json` — stay exactly as they are; mc only runs `check-wrangler.mjs --summary` as a declared note. Its deny-matrix probes in `wrangler-bump.mjs` are not reproduced in mc.

Coupling the Capacitor packages to iOS builds (`ios-release`): `mc deps` reports them like any other runtime dependency and `mc deps bump` bumps them like any other; when a bump should ride with a build is Martin's.
Disk use of workarea checkouts (~500–600 MB each under `~/mc`, the runner's `log/` and `scratch/`) — its own errand.

Major upgrades that need code changes (tiptap 2 → 3, typescript 5 → 7, jose 5 → 6, mailauth 4 → 7, stylelint 16 → 17 and the like): `mc deps` lists them under MAJOR; making the code work on them is a project of its own per package.
Transitive-only data such as `caniuse-lite` / `update-browserslist-db`, beyond what `npm audit fix --package-lock-only` changes in the `security` group.
Bumping on a schedule or from the runner: nothing in this project runs `mc deps bump` without a person typing it.
The page (`mc` with no arguments) and `mc status`: no deps section there.

success_criteria.criterion: `mc deps memoro` prints the three groups, the audit counts and the wrangler line for memoro's `origin/main`, and its counts agree with npm's own.
success_criteria.check: Run `mc deps memoro --json --refresh`; its `audit.counts` equals `metadata.vulnerabilities` from `npm audit --json --package-lock-only` run by hand in a directory holding `git -C ~/memoro show origin/main:package.json` and `…:package-lock.json`; `wrangler` appears in `security` (fix `4.149.0` or later) with `kind: "tool"` and `@capacitor/ios` with `kind: "runtime"`; `notes[0].text` starts with `wrangler `. `tests/mc/deps.test.js` green.

success_criteria.criterion: `mc deps bump` makes exactly the lockfile change a group names, in a fresh workarea, and nothing else.
success_criteria.check: `mc deps bump memoro minor --dry-run` prints each `<name> <from> → <to>` it would write and the workarea and branch it would make, and creates neither (`ls ~/mc` and `git -C ~/memoro branch --list 'deps-*'` unchanged). `tests/mc/commands/deps.test.js`: with injected git/npm/publish/merge, a bump calls npm only with `--package-lock-only`, commits only `package.json` and `package-lock.json`, and hands `mc merge` the number `mc publish` returned.

success_criteria.criterion: `mc deploy` shows the deps line from the saved reading, with its age, and says so when there is none.
success_criteria.check: `mc deploy --dry-run` after `mc deps memoro` prints a line starting `mc: deps — ` with the critical and high counts and the wrangler note; with `~/.memoro/mc/deps/memoro.json` moved away it prints `mc: deps not read — mc deps memoro`. `tests/mc/commands/deploy.test.js` green, including a test that `deployPlan` makes no npm or network call for it.

documents.label: How mc reads a repository's declaration

steps.title: `mc deps [<repo>]`: the reading, saved and printed
steps.done_when: `src/mc/deps.js` and `src/mc/commands/deps.js` exist, `deps` is in `VERB_MODULES` and in both help listings in `src/mc/help-text.js`, the memoro entry in `SHIPPED` declares the wrangler note, `normalise` carries `deps_notes`, `mc deps memoro --json --refresh` prints the reading described in the instruction and writes `~/.memoro/mc/deps/memoro.json`, and `tests/mc/deps.test.js` plus `tests/mc/help.test.js` and `tests/mc/repo-gate-table.test.js` are green.
instruction: Interface: `mc deps [<repo>] [--json] [--refresh]`. No repo means every entry of `defaultRepos(env)` (`src/mc/brief-collect.js:27`) whose `origin/main` has a `package-lock.json`. A repo is named as `mc merge` names it — resolve it with `resolveRepoPath` from `src/mc/commands/repo.js`. Register the verb in `src/mc-verbs.js` (`deps: './mc/commands/deps.js'`) and add it to both listings in `src/mc/help-text.js` (the short list near `mc deploy` at :36 and the long section near :266), or `tests/mc/help.test.js` fails ('mentions every verb either router routes'). The module exports `run(argv, deps)` and `usage()` like `src/mc/commands/shot.js`, and parses with `scanArgs` from `./flags.js` (booleans `--json`, `--refresh`). `bump` as the first positional is reserved for step 3: until then answer it with `mc: mc deps bump is not built yet` and exit 2.

The reading lives in `src/mc/deps.js`, every outside call injectable (`git`, `npm`, `now`, `runNote`) so the tests run without network — tests run under `tests/_isolate-home.mjs` and must not reach the registry. Order: `git fetch origin main --quiet` (failure is reported as `fetched: false` and the reading goes on from the refs there are), `git rev-parse origin/main`, `git show origin/main:package.json` and `:package-lock.json` into a new directory under `runnerScratchDir(env)` (`src/mc/paths.js:114`), removed in a `finally`. Then, per direct dependency (`dependencies`, `optionalDependencies`, `peerDependencies`, `devDependencies` of the manifest): `installed` from the lockfile's `packages["node_modules/<name>"].version`; `in_major` = last of `npm view <name>@^<installed> version --json` (string or ascending array); `latest` = `npm view <name> dist-tags.latest`. Run those with a concurrency of 8 (memoro has 63 direct dependencies; one `npm view` measured ~1.2 s). A package whose `npm view` fails is kept with `error` set and counted in a `failed` total — never dropped silently. Versions are compared by a local `compareVersions(a, b)` on numeric `major.minor.patch` (pre-release suffix sorts below its release); add no semver dependency.

Audit: `npm audit --json --package-lock-only` in the scratch directory (it exits non-zero when it finds anything — read stdout regardless, and fail only when stdout is not JSON). Keep `metadata.vulnerabilities` as `audit.counts`. For every entry in `vulnerabilities`: its `severity`; the direct dependencies behind it (itself when `isDirect`, else walk `effects` up to entries with `isDirect: true`, guarding against cycles); and its fix, from `fixAvailable` — `true` (fixable by `npm audit fix` within ranges), `false`, or `{ name, version, isSemVerMajor }`.

Grouping, one row per direct dependency, the first that applies: `security` when an audit entry names it as the direct dependency behind it and the fix stays inside its major (`fixAvailable === true`, or an object whose `isSemVerMajor` is false — its `version` is the row's target, e.g. wrangler → 4.149.0); `major` when `latest` is past its major (and, if the audit names it, the row carries the highest severity with `fix_crosses_major: true`); `minor` when `in_major` is newer than `installed`; otherwise current and not listed. A row carries `{ name, kind, spec, installed, target, latest, severity|null, via: [transitive names], error|null }` — `spec` is the manifest's range, `kind` is `runtime` or `tool` by the contract's rule. Transitive audit entries with `fixAvailable === true` and no non-major fix of their own are summed as `transitive_fixable` (they are what `npm audit fix --package-lock-only` changes in step 3).

Notes: a new declaration field, `deps_notes`: an array of `{ name, argv }`. Add it to `normalise` in `src/mc/repo-gate-table.js` (:416) as `Array.isArray(entry.deps_notes) ? entry.deps_notes.map(({ name, argv }) => ({ name: String(name), argv: argv.map(String) })) : []`, and to the memoro entry of `SHIPPED` as `[{ name: 'wrangler', argv: ['node', 'scripts/check-wrangler.mjs', '--summary'] }]`, with a comment saying the script is memoro's own (6 h cache in `~/.cache/memoro`, 5 s network timeout) and prints one line such as `wrangler 4.116.0 → 4.149.0 (33 minor behind; D=2 S=1)`. Read it with `declarationFor(repoPath)`; a declaration that is not `ok` gives no notes, never a failure. Each note runs with `cwd` = the primary checkout, a 20 s timeout, and keeps the first non-empty stdout line as `text`; a failure is `{ name, text: null, error }`. `tests/mc/repo-gate-table.test.js` reads the shipped entries against the repositories — run it and keep it green.

Saved: the whole reading as JSON at `join(mcHome(), 'deps', '<repo>.json')` — `{ repo, sha, read_at, fetched, audit: { counts, transitive_fixable }, groups: { security: [], minor: [], major: [] }, notes: [], failed }` — written with `writeJsonAtomic` from `src/mc/atomic-write.js`. Without `--refresh`, a saved reading for the same `sha` younger than 6 hours is printed as it is, saying its age; `--refresh` always reads anew. `--json` prints that object (an array of them when no repo was named).

Text output, English like the rest of mc: a head line `mc deps memoro — origin/main <short sha>, read <age>: <critical> critical · <high> high · <moderate> moderate`; then `SECURITY, within the major (n)`, `PATCH/MINOR (n)`, `MAJOR (n)` sections with one aligned row each — severity (security and major rows), name, `installed → target` (major: `→ latest`), `runtime`/`tool`, and `(via a, b)` for transitive causes, trimmed to three names; then `transitive: <n> more fixed by npm audit fix within ranges`; then each note's text on its own line; then `next: mc deps bump <repo> security` when the security group is not empty, else `next: mc deps bump <repo> minor` when minor is not empty. An empty group prints its heading with `(0)` and no rows.

Tests in `tests/mc/deps.test.js`, with fixtures written in the test: a manifest with one exact pin, one caret range on a 0.x and one devDependency; a lockfile v3 for them; canned `npm view` and `npm audit` outputs (audit with one direct critical whose `fixAvailable` is `true`, one direct high with `{ name, version, isSemVerMajor: false }`, and one transitive high reached through a `tool` dependency). Assert the grouping, the kinds, `via`, `compareVersions` on `0.20.2` vs `0.28.2` and `1.0.0-rc.1` vs `1.0.0`, that a failing `npm view` row is kept with `error`, that a non-JSON audit stdout fails the reading with a message naming npm audit, and that a fresh saved reading is reused without calling npm.

steps.title: `mc deploy` says the deps line from the saved reading
steps.done_when: `deployPlan` in `src/mc/commands/deploy.js` returns a `deps` field read from `~/.memoro/mc/deps/memoro.json` with no npm or network call, `planLines` prints it as the last line of the reading, `mc deploy --dry-run` shows it, and `tests/mc/commands/deploy.test.js` pins the three cases in the instruction.
instruction: `deployPlan` (`src/mc/commands/deploy.js:380`) gains an injectable `depsReading = readSavedDeps` that reads the file step 1 writes — export a reader from `src/mc/deps.js` (`readSavedReading(repo, { env })`, returning the parsed object or `null` on any read or parse failure) rather than parsing the path here. Put on the plan: `deps: reading ? { sha, short, read_at, counts: reading.audit.counts, security: reading.groups.security.length, notes: reading.notes.filter((n) => n.text).map((n) => n.text), this_tree: reading.sha === sha } : null`. No `npm`, no `fetch`, no git call for it; `--offline` changes nothing about it.

`planLines` (:450) appends one line after the nightly line. With a reading: `mc: deps — <critical> critical, <high> high<; note text…>` (each note text after `; `), followed by ` — read <age> at <short>` when `this_tree` is false and ` — read <age>` when it is true; age as whole hours or days from `read_at`. With critical and high both 0 and no notes: `mc: deps — nothing critical or high`. Without a reading: `mc: deps not read — mc deps memoro`.

The line is information and nothing else: no change to the question, the exit code, the `deploys.tsv` row or the `--json` shape beyond the added `deps` key. Update the `mc deploy` section of `src/mc/help-text.js` (:266) with one sentence that the reading ends with what `mc deps` last saved.

Tests in `tests/mc/commands/deploy.test.js` beside the existing `deployPlan` tests (:195, :214): a saved reading for the same sha gives a line with the counts and the note and no `read … at` part; one for another sha names that sha; no reading gives `mc: deps not read — mc deps memoro`; and a `depsReading` that throws is treated as no reading (wrap the call) — the deploy reading never fails for this line.

steps.title: `mc deps bump <repo> security|minor|<package>[@<version>]`: a lockfile PR through the gate
steps.done_when: `mc deps bump` makes a workarea `deps-<repo>-<what>-<yyyymmdd>` on `origin/main`, changes `package.json`/`package-lock.json` with `--package-lock-only` only, commits, publishes and runs `mc merge <repo> <pr>`; `--dry-run` prints the change and the workarea and makes neither; the help text lists it; and `tests/mc/commands/deps.test.js` pins the cases in the instruction.
instruction: Arguments: `mc deps bump <repo> <what> [--dry-run] [--json]`, `<what>` one of `security`, `minor`, or a package name with an optional `@<version>` (`wrangler`, `wrangler@4.149.0`, `@capacitor/ios@8.5.3` — split on the last `@` that is not the first character). `major` is refused: `mc: a major goes one package at a time — mc deps bump <repo> <package>@<version>`. A package that is not a direct dependency of `origin/main`'s manifest is refused by name.

First a fresh reading (`--refresh` semantics from step 1), because a bump is built on the lockfile it changes. The changes: `security` = every row of the security group to its `target`, then `npm audit fix --package-lock-only` for the transitive rest; `minor` = every row of the minor group to its `target`; a package = that package to the given version, else to its `in_major`, else (already newest in its major) refuse with `mc: <name> <installed> is the newest <major>.x — name the version to cross the major`. Nothing to change in a group: say so, exit 0, make nothing.

Writing the spec: keep the operator the manifest had. A spec with no operator (an exact pin, like memoro's `"wrangler": "4.116.0"`) goes through `npm install --package-lock-only --save-exact <name>@<version>`; `^` and `~` go through `npm install --package-lock-only <name>@<op><version>`, which npm saves as written. Batch each kind into one npm call. npm keeps a package in the section it was in; assert afterwards that every touched name is still in the same section and that `git status --porcelain` lists only `package.json` and `package-lock.json`, and stop with the list if anything else changed. Add `--ignore-scripts` to every npm call.

The workarea: name and branch `deps-<repo>-<what>-<yyyymmdd>` with `/` and `@` in `<what>` replaced by `-` (a project directory is never called `deps-…`, so `mc merge` finds no plan for it). Make it with `addWorktree({ name, repo, branch: name, from: 'origin/main', env })` from `src/mc/work-area.js:283`; an area that already exists is refused with its path. Run npm in that checkout. Commit with the message `deps(<repo>): <what> — <name> <from> → <to>, …` (the first five names, then `and <n> more`) and a body listing every change and the audit counts before. Then `mc publish` (call `run` from `src/mc/commands/publish.js` with `cwd` set to the checkout, its `--json` output parsed for `number`), then `mc merge <repo> <pr>` (call `run` from `src/mc/commands/merge.js`), passing stdout/stderr through. Its exit code is the bump's. A red gate leaves the PR open and the workarea in place, and the bump says both; `mc work tidy` removes the area once the PR has landed or closed, as for any workarea.

`--dry-run` stops before `addWorktree`: it prints the head line, one `<name> <from> → <to> (<kind>)` line per change, `transitive: <n> by npm audit fix` for security, and `would make ~/mc/<name> on origin/main and open a pull request`. `--json` prints `{ repo, what, changes, workarea, branch, pr, merged }` (pr and merged null on a dry run).

Help text: `mc deps bump <repo> <what>` in both listings in `src/mc/help-text.js`, one line saying it opens a pull request and lands it through the gate. Tests in `tests/mc/commands/deps.test.js` with injected `reading`, `addWorktree`, `npm`, `git`, `publish` and `merge`: `security` with one exact pin and one caret row makes two npm calls, both with `--package-lock-only` and `--ignore-scripts`, the exact one with `--save-exact`, then one `npm audit fix --package-lock-only`; `major` is refused; an unknown package is refused; nothing to change makes no workarea; a dirty file other than the two stops before commit; `--dry-run` calls neither `addWorktree` nor npm; and `merge` receives `[repo, String(pr)]` with the number publish returned.
